value.hook: Read before changing shared-target builds, release stamps, copy-out or deployment cleanup.
value.title: Release verification must bind the installed snapshot

sections.name: body
sections.value:
A HEAD stamp on a shared target pathname does not bind the bytes later installed: another legitimate worktree build can replace it after verification. Hold the existing build lock through copy-out into a private mktemp -d directory, verify that snapshot, and install those same bytes. In #271 the real A-build/check -> B-build -> A-install fixture and a FIFO-delayed copy proved this invariant; snapshot directories were 0700. Existing-destination checks must include both -e and -L, but check-then-copy is not atomic exclusive creation: safety relies on the private parent directory.

The stamp remains compile-time metadata, not clean-source or hermetic attestation. Dirty-input coverage must include external include_str!/include_bytes! inputs, not merely crates/manifests. Cleanup safety and cleanup completeness are separate: quote the exact owned directory; prefix filters are deletion brakes, not authentication. #271's final C34 follow-ups R271-002/R271-003 cover omitted embedded inputs and interrupted-helper leaks/unreported cleanup errors. Do not reopen them as fresh blockers without a normal-use correctness basis.

Receipt: security PASS at 8b08ba8f43726d7906076d4ef4fb2785f5472df9, output 1a2f547a776abca68c114ded6bce2f57462609e9. No real build/deploy was performed by the security seat; permission/interleaving evidence came from the independent correctness fixture.
